name: Comparative microscope tests
summary: William Dallinger tested the new Zeiss apochromatic lenses and compensating eyepieces against his best existing microscope lenses and reported a qualified verdict to British microscopists.
description: Dallinger compared Zeiss objectives and compensating eyepieces with his existing high-power lenses, including trials swapping in the new eyepieces; he and Mayall also recorded independent judgments on a supplied series.
tier_reason: Fine historical detail or an evidentiary witness; retention supports explanation without claiming broad later dependence.

impact.note: One microscopist's trial report to one society; it assessed new lenses and changed nothing later work is known to rest on.

market.note: Commercial availability is not a milestone of a scientific knowledge result.

date.basis: The tests followed the 1886 instrument introductions and preceded Dallinger’s address on 9 February 1887; exact individual test dates are not supplied.

events.statement: Dallinger compared Zeiss objectives and compensating eyepieces with his existing high-power lenses, including trials swapping in the new eyepieces; he and Mayall also recorded independent judgments on a supplied series.
events.caveats: These were reported visual comparisons with selected test objects and high-quality existing lenses, not a modern standardized quantitative trial. Dallinger’s restricted conclusions must not be generalized to all apochromats.

evidence.locator: pp. 187–188, receipt, first comparison, eyepiece substitutions and later full-series tests
evidence.supports: Actual instruments, comparison method and bounded conclusions.

links.statement: Dallinger put the compensating eyepieces on both new and existing objectives, allowing him to distinguish an eyepiece contribution from the merits of the initial Zeiss objective.
links.scope: The specific component-substitution comparison reported by Dallinger in February 1887.
links.alternatives: Ordinary eyepieces formed the initial comparator configuration.
links.caveats: This is Dallinger’s visual judgment on specified equipment, not a universal ranking of objective types.
links.timing: The 1886 eyepieces were available before the comparisons reported in early 1887.

evidence.locator: p. 188, paragraph beginning It is quite true
evidence.supports: Eyepiece substitution and bounded lack of advantage over his latest lenses.

links.statement: A Zeiss 1/8-inch objective lent through Frank Crisp, followed by a maker-supplied series, furnished the instruments Dallinger compared with his existing optics.
links.scope: Dallinger’s British comparative tests after the 1886 introduction and before 9 February 1887.
links.alternatives: His comparator set included high-quality earlier lenses; Mayall independently examined the supplied series.
links.caveats: Supplier introduction does not establish superior performance; Dallinger specifically qualifies his initial findings.
links.timing: Introduced 1886 instruments were tested before the February 1887 report; individual test dates remain unreported.

evidence.supports: Actual transfer, tested objectives and comparison results.
